granularity_note: Relevance is labelled per publication_id, not per chunk_id. Chunk-level ground truth was not labelled because the prototype corpus holds only 40 chunks across 20 publications, so chunk labels would be near-duplicates of publication labels. Retrieved chunk scores are therefore attributed to their parent publication via DISTINCT ON (publication_id).

grading_scale.3: publication is squarely about the query topic
grading_scale.2: publication is clearly related / same domain

relevance_threshold: A retrieved publication counts as relevant at grade >= 1.

corpus_fingerprint.note: All 20 publications are year 2025. Fingerprint is asserted at benchmark load time so a corpus change invalidates the labels instead of silently scoring them.

categories.natural_language: Factual questions phrased as natural language against corpus content.
categories.paraphrase: Restatements of a corpus topic in different words.
categories.conceptual: Abstract / thematic queries spanning a cluster of publications.
categories.title_entity: Titles and title fragments taken from publications themselves.
categories.negative: Strict absence: no publication in the corpus is about the topic. Every label is grade 0, so ANY returned publication is a false positive.
categories.ambiguous: Broad intent that legitimately spans multiple clusters, or labels contested on adjudication.

adjudication_policy: Negatives are labelled only where the corpus truly contains nothing. Queries that are arguably partially relevant are NOT labelled negative; they are placed in `ambiguous` with a note recording the contested judgment. See retrieval_076 ('machine learning') and retrieval_083 ('artificial intelligence').
